cues.text: Born in a refugee camp
Alphonso Davies was born in 2000 in Buduburam, a refugee camp in Ghana.
His parents, Debeah and Victoria, came from Monrovia, the capital of Liberia.
When a war came to Liberia, they had to flee.
The war forced more than 450,000 Liberians from their homes.
A refugee is someone who has to leave their home to stay safe.
Alphonso grew up in a big family, with brothers and sisters.
Light the lamp in the tent.
His story was only beginning.
Where you are born doesn’t decide where you can go. Every child deserves to feel safe.
A brand-new country
In 2005, when Alphonso was five, his family moved to Canada.
They settled in the city of Edmonton, and he started at Mother Teresa Elementary School.
Everything was new.
Later, at junior high, his school friends remembered that language was a problem for him at first, and his English was still broken.
Some classmates had also come from Liberia.
Open the school door.
Step by step, Alphonso found his way, and one teammate remembered that soccer was the thing he wanted to get into.
Being new somewhere is hard. Be patient with yourself, and ask for help when you need it.
Everyone can play
As a child, Alphonso first played organised soccer with Free Footie, an after-school league.
It was for children whose families could not afford the fees or the kit, or who had no way to get to games.
Lift the three flaps to see what Free Footie gave.
There were no fees, there was kit to wear, and a way to get to games.
Later he played for the Edmonton Internationals and the Edmonton Strikers.
Today he is an ambassador for one of his old Edmonton clubs.
When people share, everyone gets a chance. It’s okay to accept help, and one day you can help others.
Moving away at fourteen
In 2015, when he was fourteen, Alphonso moved on his own to Vancouver, far from his family, to join the Whitecaps FC Residency program.
Living away from home so young is a very big step.
Slide the suitcase to Vancouver.
In 2016, at fifteen, he signed his first professional contract, and that July he played his first Major League Soccer game.
He was the first player born in the 2000s to play in the league.
Being far from home can feel lonely. Stay in touch with the people you love, and take one brave step at a time.
Officially Canadian
Because he was born a Liberian refugee, Alphonso could not play for Canada’s national team at first.
In March 2017 he said that representing Canada was one of his dreams.
On 6 June 2017, he passed his Canadian citizenship test and became a citizen.
Stamp the passport.
One week later, at sixteen, he became the youngest player ever to play for Canada’s national team.
That summer, at the Gold Cup, he scored two goals against French Guiana, and he finished as the top scorer of the tournament.
Everyone wants to belong somewhere. A new country can become your home too.
Try again
In 2022, Canada’s men played at the World Cup for the first time since 1986.
In the first match, against Belgium, Alphonso took a penalty, and the goalkeeper saved it.
Canada lost 1–0.
Four days later, against Croatia, he tried again and scored Canada’s first ever goal at a men’s World Cup.
Kick the ball into the net.
Today he is Canada’s captain, and he was the first soccer player to become an ambassador for the United Nations refugee agency, which helps refugees around the world.
A miss is not the end. Try again, and remember where you came from.
